title: Why 250.0? Significant Figures Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A kitchen scale shows 250 g of flour. A lab balance shows 250.0 g of the same flour. Is that extra zero just decoration? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we learn what significant figures are and how they tell you how carefully something was measured.

A pencil on the live measuring bench reads 7.4 cm on a centimetre ruler and 7.43 cm on a millimetre ruler, while the readout splits sure digits from the guessed digit and the graph shows each ten times finer scale adding one significant figure. We learn the four counting rules, see link by link why front zeros never count (2.308 cm = 23.08 mm = 0.02308 m, always 4), and compare 250 g with 250.0 g side by side. Two pause-and-think questions, the rules for multiplying and adding measurements, a worked density example, the exam trap, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:

0:40 The measuring bench: cm marks vs mm marks

3:14 Rules for calculations + pause and think
3:49 Worked example: density
4:21 Exam trap: adding with the wrong rule
4:49 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
